'''Wi'ba Tuyll'''<ref name="LTFA">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref> was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] who spent time in the [[Takodana Castle|castle]] of the [[pirate]] [[Maz Kanata]] on the [[planet]] [[Takodana]]<ref name="TFA" /> around thirty [[Standard year|years]] after the [[Battle of Endor]].<ref name="TFAVD">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Tuyll was drinking at the castle's bar when Kanata, who was returning a tray of drinks to the bar beside Tuyll, recognized the [[smuggler]] [[Han Solo]] entering the establishment and cried out to him across the castle, silencing everyone present for a moment. Shortly after Solo's arrival, many of the castle's occupants were drawn outside to view the [[Hosnian Cataclysm|destruction]] of the [[Hosnian system]] by the [[First Order]]'s [[Starkiller Base]] [[superweapon]]. The First Order then [[Battle of Takodana|attacked]] and destroyed Kanata's castle. While at the castle, Tuyll wore [[Color|black]] [[boot]]s and brown [[clothing]], including a pair of [[glove]]s and a cap. His left [[eye]] was covered by an [[eye patch]] and he had fair skin and brown [[hair]].<ref name="TFA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Wi'ba Tuyll was created for the film [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']], which was released in North America on [[December 18]], [[2015]].<ref name="TFA" /> The character's appearance however, had been revealed to the public seven months earlier through an exclusive [http://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2015/05/star-wars-force-awakens-photos article] on the website of [[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair|''Vanity Fair'']].<ref name="Vanity Fair">{{WebCite|url=http://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2015/05/star-wars-force-awakens-photos|text=Adam Driver and Lupita Nyong'o's Characters Revealed in Exclusive Star Wars: The Force Awakens Photos|author=Leibovitz, Annie|date=2015-05-04|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|archivedate=20150504170503}}</ref> Tuyll was not identified in either the film or article, and would go unnamed until the released of the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' in [[2016]] in which he was one of many playable characters.<ref name="LTFA" /> Despite the game being non-[[canon]], [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] confirmed on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] that the names provided by the game for previously unidentified characters, including Tuyll, were considered canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/749616406245699584|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2016-07-03|quote=@LelalMekha Yeah, same with Infinity.|archivefile=File:PabloHidalgo-LegoName-Twitter.png|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: "@pablohidalgo <nowiki>youtube.com/watch?v=JwxAeHPLpPg</nowiki> The Lego game identifies a few BG characters from TFA, but are those names canonical?"}}</ref>
